general_information.Syllabus Name: PRINCIPLES OF ANIMATION_Nguyên lý chuyển động
general_information.Description: Description: This course takes you through the key principles of animation, which covers the '12 Principles of Animations' including: Squash & Stretch, Timing & Spacing, Solid Drawing, Anticipation, Follow Through & Overlapping Action, Arcs, Slow in & Slow out, Straight Ahead & Pose to Pose Animation, Secondary Action, Staging, Exaggeration, Appeal. This course will also provides a series of accompanying exercises to reinforce the knowledge of animation principles, including stop-motions, timelapse, flip books, etc... Objective: · Understand the 12 principles of Animations · Know how to apply the 12 principles of motion to a variety of fields including 2D Animation, 3D Animation, Interactive Media, Communication Design. · Complete an animation flipbook or paperless animation. · Complete a short Pixilation clip. · Complete a stop-motion clip
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities > - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class > - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose > - Read the textbook in advance > - Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Tools: - Internet - Microsoft word - Paper, pencil, technical pen, eraser, ruler, binder clip, lightbox, smartphone or camera, tablet, tripod, lighting lamp. - AI-assisted design tools - Photoshop, Krita, Procreate, Adobe Premiere, CapCut, Proshow Gold/Producer.v.vv

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand and recall the fundamental knowledge of the 12 principles of animation and the major types of animation.
Apply the 12 principles of animation to various contexts, including 2D animation, stop-motion animation, and pixilation.
Complete an animation flipbook or paperless animation.
Produce a short pixilation clip by applying the 12 principles of animation.
Produce a short stop-motion clip by applying the 12 principles of animation.

assessments.Duration: 1 practice/sesson 11 to sesson 24/ in class and at home
assessments.No Question: Students are required to submit the following deliverables:1. Story idea.2. Hard copy of the flipbook, properly bound and neatly finished.3. Soft copy of the flipbook, in high resolution and MP4 format, including background music, sound effects, intro, and outro.4. An additional report describing the use of AI support, if applicable.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Assessment Regulations + Assignments are first displayed and evaluated by students, then formally assessed and graded by the lecturer. + Students will receive guidance and support from the lecturer throughout the process. -AI Usage Regulations + Students are allowed to use any generative AI tools to search for secondary data and generate ideas. However, they must independently construct the final product in accordance with the conditions and requirements of the assignment. + Students must submit an AI usage report describing the process, including screenshots that illustrate the steps taken.
assessments.Note: Task 1. Students may use AI to search for script ideas, edit and present the script in a scientific manner, and support storyboard development. Tools: Can be done on paper or with graphic software such as Adobe Photoshop, Krita, etc. 2. Produce layout animation and key frames. Tools: Hand-drawn on Flipbook paper or A5–A6 paper. 3. Draw inbetweens to complete the animation product. Tools: Hand-drawn on Flipbook paper or A5–A6 paper. 4. Students present their work for instructor’s feedback and grading.
